plan.title: Add draft, commit and submit states to bh's inputs and forms
plan.description: Every form has three states. The draft: what you're typing, local to the field. Committed: the field has handed it over, on Enter, on leaving the field or the window, or after a pause in typing. Submitted: the form has sent it, on Save, or at each commit when the form saves as you go. Today bh's controls report every keystroke, so committing is each caller's: tickets' `BlurCommitInput` (`apps/web/src/registry/field-widget.tsx:19`, leaving only, no Enter or Escape, remounted with a `key` at `:100` to take a change made elsewhere), its number field's wrapper (`:116`) and `InlineTitle` (`components/item-detail.tsx`), icon-editor's `ColourPairField`, session-board's `SessionTitle`. `@bh/form` knows only submit (`onSubmit`; validation on blur and on submit). No new component: a `commit` prop on the text controls and `onCommit` beside `onSubmit` in `@bh/form`.

subtickets.title: Add `useInlineEdit`, the draft behind the prop
subtickets.description: `useInlineEdit({ value, onCommit, commit })` holds the draft and gives its handlers. It commits only a changed value; while the field isn't being edited it follows a new `value` from outside (no remount); Escape puts the committed value back. A pending pause commits at once when you leave or the field unmounts, so a draft is never lost. It stays inside bh, not exported, until a caller that isn't one of the controls needs it. `useParsedDraft` (TK-28) is the same with a parse step: build one on the other.

subtickets.title: Add `commit` to `Input`, `Textarea` and `NumberInput`
subtickets.description: `commit`: `'change'`, the default, commits every keystroke as today; `'leave'` commits on Enter, on leaving the field and on leaving the window; `{ after: 800 }` does that and also commits after 800 ms without typing. `Textarea`: Enter stays a new line. `NumberInput`: leaving the whole control commits, and a run of stepper clicks commits once. `SearchInput` and `PasswordInput` pass it to `Input`. A form or table config sets it per field as data (`{ commit: 'leave' }`).

blockedBy.why: the `commit` prop runs on `useInlineEdit`'s draft

subtickets.title: Write the controls' tests and docs
subtickets.description: Each trigger on each of the three: Enter, leaving the field, leaving the window, the pause; nothing for an unchanged value; Escape reverting; an outside change replacing the draft while idle but not while typing; a pending pause committed on leaving. The contract says a control holds no value of its own (`inputs/contract.ts`); it gets the exception: with `commit` other than `'change'` it holds a draft while you edit. A `commit` demo on each control's docs page, with the callers' cases: a field, a title, a "+ add" input.

subtickets.title: Add `onCommit` beside `onSubmit` in `@bh/form`
subtickets.description: The form has two outputs. `onCommit(change, values)` runs each time a field commits, with what changed (`{ field, value, previous }`) and the form's values after it; `onSubmit(values)` runs on Save, as today. A form uses either or both: tickets' item detail saves each field as it commits (one PATCH each) and has no Save; a create dialog sends everything on Save; a settings page can check a field as it commits and save on Save. `onCommit` may return a promise: while it runs the field shows it's saving, and if it fails the field keeps your value and shows the error. The form's values are committed values: a field's draft joins them when it commits. `commit` (when a field commits) is set per form, overridable per field, and passed to the control. Dirty means committed but not submitted: it drives "Unsaved changes", the Save button and a warning on leaving the page, so a form with no `onSubmit` is never dirty. Save while typing commits the draft first, so it isn't lost. Tests for each, and a docs page that shows a field's draft, committed and submitted values side by side as you type.

openChoices.question: When you press Escape while editing a field inside bh's drawer (an `Input` holding a draft, like tickets' item title in the item drawer), what should happen?
openChoices.context:
Today the drawer hears Escape first and closes, and the field then saves the draft as it goes away: the edit you meant to drop is kept. tickets stops that in its title by hand (TK-5.9.1). bh's fix (TK-103.1) can go two ways:

- **Drop the draft and close, in one press**: what tickets' drawer does today. For: nothing changes for the user; one small fix in the draft hook covers every `Dialog`, `Drawer` and `SidePanel`. Against: undoing a typo also closes the drawer, so you reopen it.
- **Drop the draft first, close on a second press**: the field keeps Escape while it holds a changed draft; with nothing changed, Escape closes the drawer at once. For: Escape undoes one layer at a time, as a menu open inside a drawer already does. Against: tickets' drawer behaves differently; the field has to catch Escape before the drawer, which listens early.

Drop the draft first; a second Escape closes the drawer

A query pages by skip and take by default, and by cursor as an option: every answer carries the next page's cursor, and a query may pass it back instead of `skip` (your answer: "skip/take default cursor as an option").

A stored definition (a resource's fields, a view, a template) holds no logic: field paths, text templates, filter trees and the names of renderers and formatters registered in code; a computed value such as "days open" is a field the server computes, so it filters and sorts like any other (your answer).

A field's metadata says how its value shows with a `format` (bytes, duration, percent, money…), and bh has a default renderer per kind (an option as a pill in its color, a user as an avatar and name), so a field shows the same everywhere unless a template says otherwise (your answer).
A resource's metadata names it in the singular and the plural, `label: {one: 'Item', other: 'Items'}`, so buttons, questions and counts read right from the metadata (your answer).

A field's `format` names an entry of bh's format registry, never one of a fixed list in the contract, so an app adds a format by registering it (your note on TK-11.1: "I want it to be read from format registries").

A field's kind is a name in a kind registry, as its format is, never one of a fixed set of types: bh registers nine, an app adds its own, and a field is one shape whose kind-specific `settings` its kind checks (your note on TK-11.1: "those must be also from registries so I can easily add new field type").

openChoices.question: Does `DataTable` (TK-18) load more rows as you scroll by skip and take, or by cursor?
openChoices.context:
The resource contract pages by skip and take by default, with a cursor as the option (your answer on TK-11), and TK-18.2 loads pages as you scroll.

- **By cursor**
  - For: a row added or removed above while you scroll doesn't make another show twice or go missing, and a late page costs what the first does.
  - Against: the table can't jump to a page by its number.
- **By skip and take**: the contract's default.
  - For: the simplest, the same requests a page-numbered table sends.
  - Against: tickets' items change while you read them (the board refreshes every 10 seconds today), so as you scroll a row can show twice or be skipped, and a deep page is slower.
- **As the view says**: each view (TK-16.1) picks scrolling by cursor or numbered pages by skip and take.
  - Against: `DataTable` builds both.
options: By cursor, the contract's option for a list that grows as it scrolls
By skip and take, the contract's default
As the view says: scrolling by cursor, or numbered pages by skip and take (a paging setting in TK-16.1)

openChoices.question: Where do items-core's two workflow lint rules go when it moves onto `@bh/config`?
openChoices.context:
TK-66.2 swaps items-core's `@bw/config` (its fork of bh's lint and TypeScript config) for `@bh/config`. The two differ in two rules only, both about items-core's workflow nodes (in `items-core/packages/shared/config/eslint/rules`, with their tests in `__tests__`); the rest of the difference is the `bw` → `bh` prefix and small fixes bh already has. The builder skips TK-66.2 until this is answered.

The two rules:

- **`node-file-suffix`**: a file that calls `defineNode(...)` is named `<name>.node.ts`, and the reverse.
- **`port-schema-convertible`**: inside `defineNode({ inputs, outputs, config })`, only valibot schemas that `@valibot/to-json-schema` can export.

Where they go:

- **Kept in items-core**: items-core adds the two rules on top of `@bh/config` in its own eslint config.
  - For: bh's config stays free of any one app's ideas.
- **Moved into bh**: every app gets them.
  - Against: only items-core has `defineNode`, so for the others they never fire, and bh would carry a dependency on `@valibot/to-json-schema` for them.
options: They stay in items-core: local rules in its own eslint config, on top of `@bh/config`
They move into `@bh/config`, shared by every app

epics.description:
The tickets app becomes the task system: the plans in `tasks/*.json` move into its database, the viewer's screens are rebuilt in it on bh's views, and the planner and builder work through its MCP tools. That is your answer to the direction question, under TK-80 (2026-10-12), and the plan follows it.

How the two compare, read from the code on 2026-10-12:

- **Data**: tasks/ has four fixed levels and ids that say where an item sits (`TK-11.2.1`); tickets has typed items in a scheme, a parent per item, fields of eight kinds, and keys made of a prefix and a number. Close: the plans fit a scheme of their own (TK-80.1), their ids need a stored key (TK-80.3), and GW is a prefix on both sides (TK-85).
- **State**: both have a status, with done and dropped kinds. Only tasks/ has approval as the gate to build, blockers with a why that children inherit, waits in words, `where`, and the user's own tickets. tickets' `blocks` links have no why, no inheritance and no cycle check, and its parent rollup marks a parent whose children are all cancelled as done (TK-80.2).
- **Decisions**: only tasks/ has them: questions with options, a recommended one and the answer, folded into Chosen (TK-81).
- **Notes**: tasks/ has the user's notes, the planner's replies, `seen`, and notes on a fragment of a description; tickets has comments with replies in its schema that its web never shows, reactions with no route, no read marks, and nothing on a fragment (TK-82).
- **Rules**: tasks/ checks after the fact (`pnpm tasks:check`: the schema, ids, verb-first titles, approval only on items without children, blockers, cycles); tickets' API checks every write (value types, nesting, link owners, transitions), with no rule on titles and no cycle check (TK-80.6).
- **Screens**: the viewer has the list, filters, the feature page, ticket cards, Approve and Cancel, Your decisions, the notes margin and agent chips, and reads everything every 2 seconds; tickets has project boards (a table and a kanban), item pages, All items, settings and the schema diagram, reads a project every 10 seconds, and has none of the plan's controls (TK-87).
- **Agents**: sessions change the files through `edit()`, which has no lock (TK-89); tickets' writes are commands with an id, a version check and an event, but its MCP server is broken (TK-83); agent reports live only in the viewer (TK-84).
- **Only tickets has**: history (events and an activity feed), configurable types, fields and workflows, saved views, rich text with mentions and images, and safe retries. Neither has sign-in or permissions.

The order: the plans' shape in tickets (TK-80 to TK-82), sign-in (TK-91, before approval and answers), a working MCP server (TK-83), agent reports (TK-84) and projects' repositories (TK-92) can start now; then the import, and an export of the same JSON (TK-85); then the viewer, the planner and the builder move onto tickets' API, the viewer's page unchanged (TK-86); then tickets' own screens, once bh's views reach it (TK-87, after TK-78); last, the viewer and the files go (TK-88). Until the switch the files are still the plan, and TK-89 keeps their edits from being lost. It builds on E4 to E7 rather than repeating them: the items resource (TK-13), templates and views (TK-79, TK-16, TK-19) and the `FilterBar` (TK-75).

plan.description: `/api/connections/:id/inbound` checks each payload's HMAC against the connection's secret, runs the connector's `parseInbound`, and applies the change to the local item as the connection's user, through the same commands as every other write. Older ticket: TIX-136.

plan.title: Link local items to outside objects, and stop echoing a change back
plan.description: `external_links` (connection, local item, external id, last synced hash; unique on connection and external id, and on connection and item) maps each item to its outside object. A change that came in must not be pushed straight back out: compare hashes or the actor. Older ticket: TIX-137.

plan.title: Add detecting and resolving sync conflicts
plan.description: When the local item and the outside object both changed since the last sync (by version or updatedAt), resolve by last writer wins or field by field, and record the conflict so the web can show it. A `sync_conflicts` table was sketched in July: the link, the field, the local and remote values, the resolution, when it was detected and when resolved. Older ticket: TIX-138.

plan.title: Show sync status and conflicts on a connection
plan.description: On a connection's detail: sync activity, direction and when it last synced; a list of conflicts to resolve. Reuses the run-status chip; the design prompt's Sync and Conflicts section (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-connections-ui-design-prompt.md`). Older ticket: TIX-139.

features.title: Add two-way sync with connected services: inbound webhooks, id mapping, echo suppression and conflicts
features.description: Layer 4 of the July automation roadmap, on top of the connectors (the generic HTTP one and code ones alike): changes made outside come in, and a change that came in isn't sent straight back out. The hardest layer; it needs the rules and the connectors first. Older ticket: TIX-112.

plan.title: Add Calendar to a view's modes, with the date field it places items by
plan.description: A view in calendar mode keeps its date field and the fields its chips show; the date-field picker offers only date fields. Older ticket: TIX-170.

plan.title: Build the month and week grid, with a bucket for items without the date
plan.description: Items on their day, "+N more" when a day overflows, and the items with no date in a bucket of their own. Older ticket: TIX-171.

plan.title: Add chips in the day cells, and drag to reschedule
plan.description: A chip shows the view's chosen fields and opens the item when clicked; dragging it to another day writes its date field, only where the field can be written. Older ticket: TIX-172.

plan.title: Show the calendar as an agenda list at phone width
plan.description: Items grouped by date in a list, with the same date field and chips. Older ticket: TIX-173.

features.title: Add a calendar view: items on a month or week grid by a date field
features.description: A new way to show a view: each item on the day of a chosen date field, moved to another day by dragging. Chosen in July: one date per item (no ranges), month and week, drag to reschedule, and an agenda list on a phone. Planned as E5 in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-08-configurable-views-roadmap.md` and drawn as `03b Calendar` in the claude.ai design project a75bdf6d. Views are being redone as JSON in `@bh/view` (TK-16), so the calendar is a host there or a mode of tickets' board, its chips tile templates (TK-79). The software scheme has one date field, `target_date` (`packages/db/src/seed/software-scheme.ts:73`). Older ticket: TIX-145.

plan.title: Add Timeline to a view's modes, with its start, end and row-group fields
plan.description: The start and end pickers offer only date fields; the zoom (week or month) is kept with the view. Older ticket: TIX-174.

plan.title: Build the time axis and the bars, with week and month zoom and a today line
plan.description: One bar per item from its start date to its end date, on an axis that zooms between weeks and months, with a line marking today. Older ticket: TIX-175.

plan.title: Add collapsible row groups, and color bars by status or a chosen field
plan.description: Rows grouped by the chosen field under headers that collapse; bars colored by status group or by a field the view picks. Older ticket: TIX-176.

plan.title: Let bars be dragged and resized to change their dates, and hint at dependencies
plan.description: Dragging a bar moves both dates and dragging an edge moves one, only where the fields can be written. A dashed line joins items a blocking link connects, found by what the link type means rather than its key `blocks`. Older ticket: TIX-177.

features.title: Add a timeline view: bars from a start date to an end date
features.description: A horizontal time axis with a bar per item, from a start date field to an end date field, rows grouped by a chosen field. Chosen in July: bars can be dragged and resized, and dependencies are only a hint. Planned as E6 in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-08-configurable-views-roadmap.md` and drawn as `03c Timeline` in the claude.ai design project a75bdf6d; like the calendar, it's a host or a mode on the views of TK-16. The software scheme has only one date field (`target_date`, `packages/db/src/seed/software-scheme.ts:73`), so a timeline needs a start date field as well. Older ticket: TIX-146.

plan.title: Add grouping kanban columns by any option or user field
plan.description: Grouped by status, a drop keeps to the workflow's legal moves (`apps/web/src/utils/legal-status-targets.ts`); grouped by another field, a drop sets that field's value. Get this rule right once, in `apps/web/src/components/kanban-view.tsx` or what replaces it (TK-22). Older ticket: TIX-163.

plan.title: Add swimlanes and WIP limits to the kanban board
plan.description: A second grouping draws horizontal lanes, each with a header and a count; a column may have a work-in-progress limit and shows when it's over it. Older ticket: TIX-164.

plan.title: Add Save and Reset for a view's unsaved changes
plan.description: Changes to a view's columns, sort, grouping and filters stay a draft, marked unsaved, until Save writes them to the view or Reset drops them, in place of saving each change as it's made (`apps/web/src/state/use-view-config.ts:53`). The board already keeps unsaved filters in the address until they're saved, and All items shows an unsaved dot with Reset. Older ticket: TIX-157.

features.title: Add to board views: kanban grouping by any field, swimlanes, WIP limits, and Save and Reset for changes
features.description: Three choices from the July views plan that the views rework (TK-16 to TK-22) leaves out: TK-22.1 builds kanban columns from status groups only, nothing adds lanes or limits, and TK-16.4 stores a reader's changes per view where July chose a draft that Save writes to the view. The rest of the July board work is planned: cards from a tile template (TK-22.2) and their editor (TK-20.2). Older ticket: TIX-143.

plan.title: Add editing a comment, and Edit and Delete on an item's comments
plan.description: Deleting is built on branch `tk-82` (TK-82.4: `DELETE /api/comments/:id`, by its author only, setting `deleted_at` and emitting `comment.deleted`). Add `PATCH /api/comments/:id` for its author to change the body, emitting `comment.edited`; Edit and Delete on each comment in the web (`apps/web/src/components/detail-comments.tsx`); and matching MCP tools once the MCP server works again (TK-83.1). Older ticket: TIX-86.

plan.title: Add moving an item to another project
plan.description: Today an item can only be copied and the original archived, which loses its id, its events and its comments. A move keeps the item's row, so they follow it. The item takes the next number in the target project, with its old key kept visible (or kept outright, if TK-80.3's stored key allows); its children move with it. Projects on the same scheme share types, fields and options, so only a move between schemes needs a remap by key, with a rule for a key the target lacks (refuse it, or create it). Links stay, since the API already lets a link cross projects (`apps/api/src/command/item/link.ts`). Older ticket: TIX-80.

plan.title: Add archiving a project, and deleting one with no items
plan.description: Projects can only be created and renamed (`apps/api/src/command/config/project.ts`). Add `archived_at` to `core.projects` (in the model, `packages/db/src/schema/items-platform.json`, as well as drizzle), a `project.archive` command that hides the project from the list by default, and a delete for a project with no items that removes it and its views in one transaction. An Archive action in the web, and an MCP tool beside `list_projects`. Older ticket: TIX-87.

plan.title: Delete the DEMO project from the live and dev databases
plan.description: The seeded `demo` project (prefix DEMO), a smoke test from the July Docker setup, still sits beside the real projects in the live database with 2 archived items (`Projects/tickets-backups/2026-10-13-older-projects/SUMMARY.md`, TK-85.1), and is in that backup. Remove it with the project delete above, or along with the older projects (TK-85.7 on the dev database, TK-85.8 on the live one), which remove items with their values, comments, links and events. Older ticket: TIX-79, TIX-85.

features.title: Add editing comments, moving items between projects, and archiving and deleting projects
features.description: Writes the API and the web still lack, each found in July when a fix had to be made by hand in SQL. Older ticket: TIX-104.

plan.title: Add managing an option field's options in Settings
plan.description: The API adds, renames, reorders and archives options on any option field (`POST /api/fields/:id/options`, `PATCH /api/options/:id`), but the web does it only for the workflow's statuses (`apps/web/src/components/settings/workflow-tab.tsx:186`). A field made in Settings → Fields with type `option` gets an empty option set (`apps/api/src/command/config/field.ts:29`) and no way to fill it. Add an options editor to the Fields tab. Older ticket: TIX-151.

plan.title: Replace the item screens' fixed `title`, `description`, `blocks` and `subtask` keys with what the scheme says
plan.description: The detail reads `values['title']` and a field keyed `description` (`apps/web/src/components/item-detail.tsx:119`, `:126`), marks a link as blocking only when its key is `blocks` (`detail-links.tsx:24`), and adds children as type `subtask` (`detail-children.tsx:151`, `new-item-dialog.tsx:25`). The plan scheme's child type is `subticket` (branch `tk-80`, `packages/db/src/seed/plan-scheme.ts`), so "Add subtask" finds no type there. Find the title and description by their role with a fallback, a blocking link by what its link type means, and the child type from the parent type's allowed children (`structure.item_type_child_types`): that part is TK-80.12, needed for the plans first. Older ticket: TIX-180.

features.title: Make Settings and the item screens work with any scheme, not only the software one
features.description: Two places where the web assumes the seeded software scheme. Both matter more now that a plan scheme (TK-80.1) sits beside it. Older ticket: TIX-151, TIX-180.

features.title: Update the API and MCP docs pages to today's routes
features.description: Eight pages in `docs/api` and `docs/mcp` still describe the old `/api/tickets` routes, which were replaced by `/api/items` and the project routes. Found while triaging the older TIX tickets; no ticket asked for it.
